# Parthenon. West pediment. Poseidon

## Identity and consulted witness

Acropolis Museum, “Parthenon. West pediment. Poseidon,” inventory Ακρ. 885, accessed September 8, 2026. [Selected digital carrier](https://www.theacropolismuseum.gr/en/node/23827). Accessed and saved 8 September 2026. The raw response is retained at `working/sources-texts-references/primary-texts/attica/acropolis-museum-west-pediment-poseidon.html` (SHA-256 `cfe1570bd1fd89319cab81a28d115ad3731a3e089077dcd5c3fc483639057465`). A saved page can contain more material than the selected reading; no whole-work reading is claimed.

## Source-specific reading

The museum identifies the object as Ακρ. 885, dates it to 437–432 BCE, and describes surviving fragments and their reconstruction. It proposes two readings of the raised trident: withdrawing it after producing the spring, or striking to inundate the city. Its wider scene places local kings, heroes and river figures around the divine contest.

This is modern object interpretation with surviving material and reconstruction distinguished. The local-hero judgment described by the museum cannot be inserted into Pseudo-Apollodorus’s expressly different tribunal. The bibliography is a research route, not a list of works consulted in this admission.
